# Dev Catalog

> A curated, rated catalog of useful developer scripts, tools, and workflows. Every entry records where it came from, its license, the platforms it runs on, what it requires, and a curator rating.

Full metadata for every entry is in [catalog/index.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/catalog/index.json). Install steps by entry type are in the [install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/skills/dev-catalog/references/install.md). Repository: https://github.com/alex-red/dev-catalog

Rubric (dev-v1): seven 0–4 grades weighted by practical value 25%, dependability 20%, ease of use 15%, safety and control 15%, adoption cost 10%, portability 10%, upkeep 5%; weighted total / 40 gives a score out of 10. Higher is better on every axis. Missing grades produce no score. See the [rating guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/docs/ratings.md). Within each section, complete ratings come first, then incomplete ones, then entries with blockers. Evidence: reviewed, used, tested. Select for fit first, and never let a high score clear a blocker. Read a script before running it.

## Scripts

- [Prune merged local Git branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/git-prune-merged/SCRIPT.md): A dry-run-first Bash script that lists local branches already merged into the default branch and deletes them on --delete. It finds the default branch from origin/HEAD and never touches the base, the current branch, or branches checked out in a worktree. Use when: Local branches have piled up after merged pull requests and you want to clear the ones that are safely merged without guessing. — id `git-prune-merged`, 8.6/10, evidence tested, platforms macos/linux, requires git, bash, tags git, branches, cleanup, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/git-prune-merged/entry.yaml)
- [Reclaim disk space from developer caches and build output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/disk-reclaim/SCRIPT.md): An interactive Bash script that finds reclaimable space in developer caches, build output, idle projects, Docker, temp dirs and the Trash. It lists sizes by risk and asks before cleaning selected items. Direct file deletion checks local paths, and external cleaners manage their own stores. Use when: A development machine is running low on disk and you want to see which caches, node_modules, build outputs and leftovers are worth clearing before deleting anything. — id `disk-reclaim`, 8.4/10, evidence tested, platforms macos/linux, requires bash, tags cleanup, disk-space, caches, cli, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/scripts/disk-reclaim/entry.yaml)

## Workflows

- [Work on parallel Git branches with worktrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/git-worktree-parallel/WORKFLOW.md): Keep a feature checkout open while reviewing another branch or handling a hotfix in a separate directory. Set up project dependencies there and clean up with Git when the task is done. Use when: You need another branch checked out alongside work in progress, especially when switching branches would interrupt a dev server or trigger a rebuild. — id `git-worktree-parallel`, 9.6/10, evidence reviewed, platforms any, requires git, tags git, branches, environment-setup, original, informed by https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/git-worktree-parallel/entry.yaml)
- [Find a regression with git bisect run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/git-bisect-regression/WORKFLOW.md): A step-by-step method for finding the commit that introduced a regression, using an automated check script with git bisect run. Covers exit-code semantics, skipping unbuildable commits, flaky checks, merge-heavy history, and keeping a record. Use when: Something worked in an older version and fails now, and reading recent diffs has not shown the cause. — id `git-bisect-regression`, 9.1/10, evidence reviewed, platforms any, requires git, tags git, debugging, regression, original, informed by https://git-scm.com/docs/git-bisect, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/git-bisect-regression/entry.yaml)
- [Diagnose failed CI browser tests with Playwright traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/playwright-ci-traces/WORKFLOW.md): Record traces selectively in Playwright Test, save the HTML report as a CI artifact, and inspect the failed action alongside the DOM, console, and network activity. Use when: A Playwright test fails in CI and screenshots or logs alone do not explain what happened. — id `playwright-ci-traces`, 8.8/10, evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, requires Node.js, npm, Playwright Test (@playwright/test), tags debugging, testing, playwright, original, informed by https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/workflows/playwright-ci-traces/entry.yaml)

## Tools

- [bat syntax-highlighting file viewer](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/tree/979ba22628bc9d8171f2cffca2bd5c90c9fc0a9e): Read text files in the terminal with syntax highlighting, optional line numbers and Git change markers, and automatic paging. Use when: You regularly read code, configuration, or logs from the terminal or want syntax-highlighted fzf previews. — id `bat`, 10.0/10, evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, tags cli, navigation, linked from https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/tree/979ba22628bc9d8171f2cffca2bd5c90c9fc0a9e, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/tools/bat/entry.yaml)
- [dust ranked directory sizes](https://github.com/bootandy/dust/tree/079c55266917387e416e0f871c97c06da52df12d): Summarize disk usage as a tree with size bars so the largest paths stand out. Limit depth or change what gets counted when investigating a large tree. Use when: You want a quick answer to which files or subdirectories account for most of the space under a path. — id `dust`, 10.0/10, evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, tags cli, disk-space, linked from https://github.com/bootandy/dust/tree/079c55266917387e416e0f871c97c06da52df12d, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/tools/dust/entry.yaml)
- [fd for finding files by name](https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/tree/193d0df1d0ad455e44506953a2cd80428203ff35): Find paths by name, extension, or file type with short commands. Respects ignore rules and skips hidden entries by default. Use when: You search for paths in source trees or need a file list for a picker, watcher, or another command. — id `fd`, 10.0/10, evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, tags cli, search, linked from https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/tree/193d0df1d0ad455e44506953a2cd80428203ff35, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/tools/fd/entry.yaml)

Use when: You maintain Bash or POSIX shell scripts and want actionable diagnostics before local runs or CI. — id `shellcheck`, 10.0/10, evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, tags cli, linting, linked from https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/tree/aac0823e6b58f8a499e856e93738082691cbf212, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/tools/shellcheck/entry.yaml)
- [fzf fuzzy finder](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/tree/c0a193e031f01fb50bf6f7be4381990a3753f7cf): Interactively filter files, shell history, or any list piped into the terminal. Select one or more matches for use in another command. Use when: You repeatedly scroll through shell history, navigate long lists, or write shell helpers that need a keyboard-driven picker. — id `fzf`, 9.6/10, advisories: [CVE-2026-115319](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2026-115319) (Optional HTTP server on affected builds). A crafted request can stall the HTTP server. File and history picking work with --listen and --listen-unsafe off. Use a patched build if you need the server., evidence reviewed, platforms macos/linux/windows, tags cli, search, linked from https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/tree/c0a193e031f01fb50bf6f7be4381990a3753f7cf, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/dev-catalog/main/entries/tools/fzf/entry.yaml)

A drop-in for most grep -r uses.
